en: The Ritual for the Recitation of the Bodhisattva Mahāgaganagañja.
By the Grand Master of State Affairs, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Duke of Sū State with a Fief of Three Thousand Households, conferred the purple robe and posthumously titled Minister of Works, Grand Mirror (Dajian).
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Temple, who possesses Great and Vast Wisdom, in accordance with an Imperial Edict:
I shall now, based upon the Yoga Vajraśekhara Sūtra, expound the mantra teachings of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha of the Ratna Family.
Out of compassion for those living at home and those in the mountains who possess little merit or virtue and lack sufficient resources—
whose worldly and supramundane superior aspirations for what they seek are mostly not fulfilled according to their wishes.
If one practices according to these teachings,
all obstacles such as karmic retribution will be completely eliminated;
merit and virtue will increase, and the mind and spirit will become joyful and at ease.
Possessing pure faith in the Mahāyāna, they bring benefit and happiness to sentient beings with a mind free from regression,
and they shall obtain all worldly and transcendental wealth and treasures.
They are able to bring benefit to all sentient beings;
even the mass of merit obtained from a single recitation or a single thought is as vast as space,
let alone when one intentionally practices according to the Dharma.
One’s aspirations will certainly be fulfilled with supreme accomplishment.
The practitioner should first enter the mandala of empowerment and personally receive the ritual procedures from before the Master.
Whether in a quiet place among the mountains or in a monastery,
in whatever location one prefers,
one should establish a meditation chamber and construct an altar for a single direction.
According to their size,
smear the ground with *gomaya* and construct eight maṇḍalas.
Banners are suspended all around,
with celestial canopies placed above;
on the western side of the altar, an image of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha is installed.
The practitioner should perform the recitation facing the image at the eastern side of the maṇḍala.
One should scatter various seasonal flowers upon the maṇḍala and offer incense, lamps, food, and fruit.
He made offerings according to what his means permitted.
Whenever he entered the dharma hall,
he prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground before the honored image.
Having paid homage to all Tathāgatas and the assembly of noble ones,
and having performed confession, rejoicing in merit, requesting [the turning of the wheel], and making vows,
one then sits in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
Or, sitting in the half-lotus posture as one pleases, with body upright and mindfulness established,
one should apply fragrant ointment to both hands and join the palms with hollowed centers like an unfurled lotus flower.
Recite the Mantra of Purity three or seven times and perform the mudrā of scattering over the crown of the head;
thus, the three karmas are purified, thereby accomplishing the ultimate bath.
The mantra for purifying the three karmas is as follows:
Oṃ śūnyatājñānagarbha svāhā. Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Heart of the Buddha Family by means of the ten perfections of śamatha and vipaśyanā.
Crossing the hands within, form fists;
then extend the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers together to complete the mudrā.
Visualize all Buddhas pervading the expanse of space,
and then recite the Heart Mantra of the Buddha Family three times.
The mantra for the mudrā of scattering [flowers] upon the crown of the head is as follows:
Oṃ īṃ īṃ kaḥ svāhā. Next, form the heart-samaya mudrā of the Lotus Family, following the same procedure as the heart mudrā of the Buddha Family mentioned previously.
Having bent the *jñāna-pāṇi* (wisdom-hand) into the palm and straightened the *dhyāna-pāṇi* (meditation-hand),
one forms this mudrā.
Visualize that to the right of all Tathāgatas are the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and his retinue.
Recite the heart-mantra of the Lotus Family three times while forming the mudrā.
The mantra for the mudrā of scattering at the crown on the right is:
Oṃ āḥ lūṃ ka phaṭ svāhā. Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Vajra Family Heart.
Following the preceding Heart Seal of the Buddha Family,
bend the Dhyāna-pāramitā finger inward into the palm and extend the Prajñā-pāramitā finger straight upward.
Visualize that to the left of all the Tathāgatas are the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi and his retinue;
then recite the heart-mantra of the Vajra Family three times.
The mantra for the mudrā of scattering at the crown of the head is:
Oṃ vajra-tīkṣṇa svāhā. Next, perform the armor-binding mudrā to protect the body.
Visualize the dhyāna-pāramitā as a feather held across the palm.

With the four pāramitās of vīrya, kṣānti, śīla, and dāna, clench the fist to form this mudrā, sealing the five places of the body: namely, the forehead, the right shoulder, the left shoulder, the heart, and the throat.
This is called the mantra for protecting the five places.
It is: Oṃ pūṃ jvala hūṃ. By forming this mudrā and consecrating the five places with it, one immediately becomes armored in the firm mail of vajra-flame radiance.
No māras whatsoever shall be able to create obstacles or difficulties;
the mantra one upholds will swiftly attain accomplishment.
Next, form the mudrā for inviting the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha.
Form the Vajra-bond with both hands;
extend the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers straight upward,
then curve them inward so they resemble the shape of a jewel.
The advancing forces each bend like a hook.
Visualize a precious pavilion within the maṇḍala;
inside the pavilion is an eight-petaled lotus flower in full bloom.
Recite the mantra four times.
With the power of exertion, beckon them toward yourself;
the deity and their retinue will all assemble.
The mantra for the invitation is:
Oṃ sarvatathāgataviśvakarmavajraratna sarvāśāparipūrakāya hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ traṃ. Next, perform the mudrā of the body of Kuntalī.
Place the left hand beneath the right with the palms facing upward;
interlace the fingers so they enter the hollows of the palms.
Then, place the square [right] hand over the top, pressing down upon the intersection.
With dhyāna and prajñā, both press against the square of the precepts;
with kṣānti and praṇidhāna, they stand upright, their heads supporting one another;
vīrya and bala are bent like a hook.
Form the shape of a three-pronged vajra and recite the mantra of Kuṇḍalī; as you recite it,
perform the mudrā accordingly.
Circumambulate three times to the left to dispel all māras.
Circumambulate three times to the right, and then recite the mantra for binding the boundary (*sīmābandha*):
*Namo ratnatrayāya | namo vajrakrodhāya | oṃ hulu hulu tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bandha bandha hana hana amṛte hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* Next, offer the *argha* water.
The practitioner should always place two clean vessels near his knees upon the altar,
filled with scented water to serve as argha.
When first inviting [the deity], one offers on the right side;
when later escorting [the deity] away, one offers on the left side.
At each time of making an offering, one holds the arghya vessel with both hands.
Offer it upon the forehead.
Then, reciting the mantra while visualizing the bathing of the principal deity and the assembly of holy beings, the mantra is:
Oṃ vajranāga hūṃ. Next, perform the mudrā for offering the lotus seat.
With both hands, join the palms with the hollows facing upward;
touch the tips of the thumbs (dāna) and the little fingers (prajñā) together,
while the remaining six fingers of the middle [sections] are slightly bent.
The heads are separated like the petals of a blooming lotus. The mantra is:
Oṃ kamala svāhā. By binding this mudrā and consecrating it with this mantra, [the rite is accomplished].
All the assembly of noble ones, together with their respective tutelary deities,
shall each obtain a seven-jeweled lotus flower as a seat.
Next, form the Great Ākāśagarbha Seal for Universal Offering.
Join the two palms together.
Bind the fingers of the two *śīla* (ring) fingers outward.
With the two *vīrya* (middle) fingers, bend them back toward the palm in the shape of a jewel.
Having completed the formation of the mudrā,
recite the mantra four times.
The mantra for universal offering is as follows:

Oṃ gaganasampravartta vajra hūṃ. Visualize that from the mudrā there arise immeasurable varieties of offerings: incense, flowers, lamps, unguents, food and drink, precious banners, flags, and canopies.
Thereby, one accomplishes a truly vast and sublime offering before the principal deity and all the assembly of noble ones.
Next, one binds the karma-mudrā.
Place the *śamatha* fingers against the heart with the palms facing upward;
join the *prajñā* fingers together,
bending them back at the joints so that they form the shape of a jewel.
Visualizing the palms facing upward like outspread wings, perform the mudrā of the wish-granting gesture (*varada-mudrā*) by extending them forward; having bound this seal, reflect thus:
"My own body is identical to the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha. Then, recite the karma-mantra as follows:
Oṃ vajra-ratna-bīja-haṃ. By means of this visualization and empowerment, the practitioner’s own body becomes identical to the deity Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva.
Next, bind the samaya-mudrā:
with both hands in the vajra-bond,
extend the forefingers and curl them back toward the palms in the shape of a jewel.
Holding the meditation and wisdom [mudrās] upright together at the heart, one recites the samaya mantra seven times. The mantra is:
Oṃ vajraratna hūṃ. Then, taking a crystal rosary, one places it within the palms.
Place the palms together at the heart and recite the mantra for empowering the rosary three times. The mantra is:
Oṃ virujan-māla svāhā. Then, holding the rosary, place it upon the crown of the head.
He made this aspiration, saying:
"May all those who cultivate the practice of mantras throughout the worlds of the ten directions,
and all the mantras they uphold,"
"May it be swiftly accomplished. Then,
he stops the feather and holds the bead,
visualizing the feather at his heart.
Moving the beads neither too slowly nor too hurriedly,
with the mind free from distraction,
one completes the limit of the count, whether it be a thousand or a hundred.
Holding the jewel to his crown, he further made this aspiration:
"May all sentient beings obtain whatever they desire—
the sublime fruits of both the mundane and supramundane realms."
"By the power of the merit of my recitation,
may [this] be swiftly accomplished.
Then, he placed the jewel back in its original location.
Again, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Honored One and recite the Samaya-mantra seven times;
then release the mudrā over the crown of the head.
Furthermore, form the seal of universal offering and recite the mantra of universal offering seven times.
Then, dispersing the seal from the crown of the head, recite the praise to the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha as follows:
1. Vajra-ratna-svabhāva-vajra-rata | 2. Vajra-karṣa-mahā-mani-ākārṣaya vajra-tarpaṇa | 3. Vajra-tarpaṇa-namo-stute | Having recited this hymn of praise, [proceed].
Then, take the argha water from the left side and offer it to the forehead.
Immediately, form the previously mentioned khaṭvāṅga mudrā.
Rotate [the mudrā] once counter-clockwise to dissolve the boundary.
Next, bind the samaya-mudrā and bid farewell to all the noble assemblies.
The mantra for respectfully presenting [the offering] is:
Oṃ vajraratna muḥ. Forming the mudrā, place it upon the crown of the head and recite the mantra seven times.
This constitutes the offering and escorting of all the noble assemblies.
Then, bind the heart-samaya mudrās of the three families, reciting each three times.
Next, bind the protection-of-the-body mudrā.
As before, seal the five places;
then, prostrating to the Buddha and making vows as desired, exit the maṇḍala.
Recite Mahāyāna sūtras and seal stūpas with the Buddha-seal.
One should extensively practice the giving of alms and constantly benefit all sentient beings.
This is the *Dhāraṇī Recitation Method of the Bodhisattva Mahāgaganagañja*.
